The exact two-file diff upgrades cargo-zigbuild and replaces a fixed test sleep with bounded polling and exact status verification.

properties.claim: Rust 1.98 and Zig 0.16 can build every Linux release target in the workflow when cargo-zigbuild 0.23.2 is used.

oracle.observes: successful linker completion and an emitted ELF for each of the four Linux release targets
oracle.layer: real Rust, Zig, and cargo-zigbuild toolchain
oracle.method: build all four workflow targets and inspect each output artifact

proxy_challenge.proxy: cargo-zigbuild 0.23.2 source contains the expected filter
proxy_challenge.counterexample: the filter could exist while the project still fails to link due to another Rust 1.98 or Zig 0.16 incompatibility
proxy_challenge.evidence: All four project targets linked successfully, so the source-level filter is not the sole oracle.

substrates.evidence: Both ARM64 release builds emitted valid AArch64 ELF artifacts.

substrates.name: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.2.28 and x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
substrates.evidence: Both x64 release builds emitted valid x86-64 ELF artifacts.

properties.evidence: The four real release builds passed with rustc 1.98.0, Zig 0.16.0, and cargo-zigbuild 0.23.2.

properties.claim: The dependency upgrade preserves the release artifact compatibility contract: GNU binaries require no GLIBC newer than 2.28 and musl binaries remain static.

oracle.observes: ELF linkage mode, architecture, interpreter, and referenced GLIBC symbol versions
oracle.method: inspect all four ELF artifacts with file and scan the GNU version requirements

proxy_challenge.proxy: the workflow target name still includes .2.28 or musl
proxy_challenge.counterexample: a successful build could silently link a GNU symbol newer than 2.28 or make a musl artifact dynamic
proxy_challenge.evidence: Artifact inspection, rather than target naming, showed GLIBC_2.28 as the GNU maximum and static linkage for both musl outputs.

substrates.name: GNU ARM64 and x64 ELF outputs
substrates.evidence: Both are dynamic for their expected architecture and reference no GLIBC version above 2.28.

substrates.name: musl ARM64 and x64 ELF outputs
substrates.evidence: Both artifacts are reported as statically linked.

properties.evidence: The artifact corpus preserved the workflow's architecture and libc compatibility promises.

properties.claim: The Unix child-exit test tolerates scheduler delay, remains bounded, observes the exact exit code 42, and does not intentionally orphan the child on timeout.

oracle.observes: the real child process status returned by std::process::Child::try_wait
oracle.method: run immediate and one-second-delayed real child exits, mutate back to the fixed-sleep defect, repeat the delayed case 100 times, and run the full suite

proxy_challenge.proxy: the test passes once with an immediate child exit
proxy_challenge.counterexample: the scheduler can keep the child live past a fixed sleep even though an immediate isolated run passes
proxy_challenge.evidence: The one-second delayed producer made the fixed-sleep implementation fail at the intended assertion, while bounded polling passed it 100 of 100 times.

substrates.name: real macOS /bin/sh child process
substrates.evidence: Command spawned /bin/sh, immediate and delayed exits produced status code 42, and the final narrow test passed again.

substrates.name: full macOS x64 Rust CI-equivalent suite
substrates.evidence: 1,145 tests passed, 101 were ignored, and both doctor integration tests passed.

properties.evidence: The old timing assumption was forced red; the deadline-polling implementation was restored green and survived 100 delayed repetitions.

values: producer timing: immediate exit or exit after one second
pre-observation state: child still running or already exited
observation: try_wait returns None while live and Some(status) after exit
schedule sample: isolated run, 100 repeated delayed runs, and full-suite contention
exclusions: a permanently non-exiting child is outside this regression test's exit-detection contract; the ten-second deadline is harness cleanup and its branch explicitly kills and waits before failing
Windows is excluded by the existing cfg(unix) contract and /bin/sh producer
dimensions.evidence: The model covers the scheduler-delay family that caused CI to return None after 200 ms and the exact status transition the test promises to observe.

oracle.source: operating-system child status from a real /bin/sh producer
oracle.evidence: Expected status 42 comes from the shell command, not from the polling implementation.

producer.name: std::process::Command spawning /bin/sh
producer.evidence: The narrow test, delayed mutation, 100-run campaign, and full suite all used the real process producer.

falsification.mutation: change the child to sleep 1; exit 42 and restore the old fixed 200 ms sleep implementation
falsification.red_evidence: The test failed at the intended assertion: try_wait() returned None but child should have exited.
falsification.restored_green_evidence: Deadline polling passed the same delayed producer, then passed 100 of 100 repetitions and the final immediate source.

behavioral_strength.evidence: The test rejects the exact timing-assumption defect, reaches a real OS process boundary, and is deterministic under repeated delay.

assumptions.source: failed release job and upstream cargo-zigbuild patch
assumptions.claim: Rust 1.98's new Cortex-A53 linker argument is the cause of both ARM64 release failures.
assumptions.evidence: The failed job passes the exact unsupported argument through cargo-zigbuild 0.22.3, and upstream filters that exact value in 0.23.2.

assumptions.claim: The macOS failure is a scheduler timing assumption rather than a broken try_wait contract.
assumptions.evidence: CI failed only because try_wait returned None after the fixed sleep; a real delayed child reproduces that state, then deadline polling observes exit 42.

assumptions.claim: No product documentation needs updating because neither change alters a user-facing command or runtime contract.
assumptions.evidence: The diff only changes the release build tool version and a cfg(test) function.

side_effects.evidence: The diff itself publishes nothing and changes no production runtime path; release publication still requires merge and the existing main-branch workflow, while the process change is confined to cfg(test).
